title: Efficient Rectification Signal Validation for Optimal Functional ECO Patch Generation
problem: Synthesis-based functional ECO (Engineering Change Order) patch generation requires identifying optimal rectification signals from candidates; signal validation step is often ad hoc and inefficient.
motivation: Functional bug fixes via ECO often focus on patch generation (step 2) while neglecting systematic rectification signal collection and validation (step 1), leaving performance on the table.
method: Starting with candidate electrical signals that could fix the chip bug, the framework systematically gathers all possible combinations and tests which ones actually work. A ranking heuristic prioritizes combinations likely to work while keeping the total number of signals minimal. The framework then feeds the validated signal combinations into existing chip-patch generation tools.
key_novelty: Instead of manually selecting signals, the approach systematically ranks and validates all candidate signal combinations to find the smallest working fix.
contributions: Heuristic for identifying high-quality rectification signal candidates
Efficient algorithm for validating all feasible rectification signal sets
Signal grouping and ranking technique ensuring minimal patch generation
limitations: Evaluation focused on patch size; timing closure, routability impact, or area overhead not discussed.
primary_theme: Systematic rectification signal validation for ECO
